basis: Lilly lost-horse judgment: the horse is signified by the lord of the twelfth, and that lord is retrograde and hastening to a conjunction of the lord of the querent's second house (his substance/possessions) — retrogradation is return, and the horse's significator applying to conjoin the lord of the owner's goods is the classic testimony that the lost beast comes back into the owner's possession. Corroboration stacks on the second house: the Moon is locally in the second, and two retrograde planets are near the cusp of the second — multiple return-testimonies gathered at the house of recovery. Direction is taken by sign testimony: the sign of the twelfth and the sign wherein its lord is placed are both west, and the plurality of testimonies is full west, so the horse went westward. The seventh house afflicted concerns the thief/taker's ill condition, not the recovery, which is already perfected by the applying conjunction. Verdict: recoverable, from the west.
prediction_text: The horse is recoverable and will be recovered: the lord of the twelfth (the horse) is retrograde — the sign of return — and hastens to a conjunction with the lord of the querent's second house of substance, with the Moon in the second and two retrogrades at its cusp, so the horse comes back into its owner's possession. And it went west: the sign of the twelfth and the sign holding its lord are both west, the plurality of testimonies full west — let him seek westward from Henley.
timing: Day-to-week scale (a lost beast, near at hand): window of the coming days to few weeks while the lord of the twelfth completes his conjunction with the lord of the second; main coordinate at that conjunction, in the nearer part of the window
